page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration consists of 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 7430.34 and a Passmark CPU score of 8305.34. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1138.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1409.67. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 412.9 GB/sec for cached reads and 48.32 GB/sec for uncached reads. The server handles static web serving at 6.62 GB/sec and processes Redis SET operations at 7.13 million operations per second. Small-scale LLM inference runs at 415.57 tokens per second for prompt processing and 115.93 tokens per second for text generation using a 135M model.

The n2-highcpu-8 offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources without the overhead of large memory allocations. The 1.0 GB per vCPU ratio represents a clear tradeoff: while it reduces costs for compute-heavy tasks, it is highly constrained for memory-intensive applications, as reflected in its weak Passmark memory score of 1328.72.

This server is suited for multi-threaded CPU-bound tasks that do not require substantial memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include software compilation, text processing, static web serving, and lightweight database operations. It is also capable of handling small-scale language model inference and basic multi-threaded decompression tasks.
